custom_variables.value: Last note on AI agents for marketing

custom_variables.name: body1
custom_variables.value:
Adam,

I saw Vagabond's recent runway activity and the A/W content on The Shoemakers Journal - great work bringing product stories to life. As Project Manager Digital Marketing, you’re likely juggling seasonal campaigns, social, and localization for DACH/Nordics.

You downloaded a guide about AI agents for marketing - I’d love 15 minutes to show 2 AI workers that can speed content production (social/video/email) and localize campaigns while keeping your brand voice consistent.

Best,

custom_variables.name: body2
custom_variables.value:
Adam,

Quick follow-up - many fashion marketing teams struggle to turn runway and editorial content into localized ads and email quickly. A social+video repurpose AI worker could turn runway footage and Shoemakers Journal copy into short social videos, captions, and localized email lines in minutes.

If you have 10 minutes I can show a sample workflow built for a seasonal drop. Is Tuesday or Thursday better next week?

Thanks,

custom_variables.name: body3
custom_variables.value:
Adam,

Since Vagabond is active with seasonal editorial and social, a simple pilot can deliver ready-to-run assets for DACH/Nordics fast. Teams using Marketing AI workers report much faster content velocity and more consistent localization across markets.

Would you like a 2-slide sample showing how we’d turn one A/W story into 8 social assets + 2 emails for your channels? I can send it over today.

Regards,

custom_variables.name: body4
custom_variables.value:
Adam,

If now isn’t the right time, no problem - should I send the 2-slide sample to you or someone on your team instead? Happy to wait or follow up later.

Best,

Best,
Hanna

Best,

Based on what you’re running today (Market Intelligence + webinars), the idea would be to start with one focused use case:

turning a single webinar or research piece into a structured follow-up and distribution workflow.

- generating segmented follow-ups and content outputs

thread.subject: Re: Double meetings without more headcount
thread.text:
Hey David,

That actually makes total sense - and honestly, you’re already in a pretty clean setup (Apollo + HubSpot is a good base, I use it too :) ).

Where we usually come in is not by adding *more tools*, but by turning what you already have into a system that actually runs:

- deciding who to reach out to and how

- personalizing messaging based on signals

- triggering outreach + follow-ups automatically

So instead of “more outbound effort,” it becomes a bit more like *managed outbound*.

Out of curiosity - what’s the biggest bottleneck for you right now?

Is it more around:

- finding the right people

- writing custom messages per each lead

- or staying consistent with follow-ups?

Happy to show you how this could look in your setup if helpful - nothing heavy, just a quick walkthrough.

Hanna

[Book a meeting](https://calendly.com/hanna-l-everworker/30-minutes-to-chat)

thread.text:
Hey David,

That actually makes total sense - and honestly, you’re already in a pretty clean setup (Apollo + HubSpot is a good base, I use it too :) ).

Where we usually come in is not by adding *more tools*, but by turning what you already have into a system that actually runs:

- deciding who to reach out to and how

- personalizing messaging based on signals

- triggering outreach + follow-ups automatically

So instead of “more outbound effort,” it becomes a bit more like *managed outbound*.

Out of curiosity - what’s the biggest bottleneck for you right now?

Is it more around:

- finding the right people

- writing custom messages per each lead

- or staying consistent with follow-ups?

Happy to show you how this could look in your setup if helpful - nothing heavy, just a quick walkthrough.

Hanna

thread.subject: Re: Lower CAC and speed creative
thread.text:
Hi Dan,

Yep - makes sense, let me give you something more concrete.

Most teams we work with fall into a few typical setups depending on what they’re trying to scale:

1. Focused use case (e.g. content + landing pages)
- 1-2 AI Workers
- typically in the $2-4k/month range
- used to increase output speed and test more variations without adding workload

2. Growth layer (content + campaigns + basic automation)
- 2-4 AI Workers
- usually around $5-9k/month
- covers content production, campaign execution, and some reporting/iteration

3. Full workflow (end-to-end growth support)
- 4+ AI Workers
- typically $10k+ / month
- used when teams want to run multiple channels and automate a bigger part of execution

The right setup really depends on where you’re trying to move the needle (CAC, volume, speed, etc.), so these are just benchmarks.

If helpful, we can quickly map this to what Wype is doing today and narrow it down to a much tighter range - no more than 15 mins.

Warmly,

Hanna Liakh

[Book a meeting](https://calendly.com/hanna-l-everworker/30-minutes-to-chat)

thread.subject: Re: Lower CAC and speed creative
thread.text:
Hi Dan,

Yep - makes sense, let me give you something more concrete.

Most teams we work with fall into a few typical setups depending on what they’re trying to scale:

1. Focused use case (e.g. content + landing pages)
- 1-2 AI Workers
- typically in the $2-4k/month range
- used to increase output speed and test more variations without adding workload

2. Growth layer (content + campaigns + basic automation)
- 2-4 AI Workers
- usually around $5-9k/month
- covers content production, campaign execution, and some reporting/iteration

3. Full workflow (end-to-end growth support)
- 4+ AI Workers
- typically $10k+ / month
- used when teams want to run multiple channels and automate a bigger part of execution

The right setup really depends on where you’re trying to move the needle (CAC, volume, speed, etc.), so these are just benchmarks.

If helpful, we can quickly map this to what Wype is doing today and narrow it down to a much tighter range - no more than 15 mins.

Warmly,

Hanna Liakh

thread.subject: Re: Lower CAC and speed creative
thread.text:
Hi Dan,

Yep - makes sense, let me give you something more concrete.

Most teams we work with fall into a few typical setups depending on what they’re trying to scale:

1. Focused use case (e.g. content + landing pages)
- 1-2 AI Workers
- typically in the $2-4k/month range
- used to increase output speed and test more variations without adding workload

2. Growth layer (content + campaigns + basic automation)
- 2-4 AI Workers
- usually around $5-9k/month
- covers content production, campaign execution, and some reporting/iteration

3. Full workflow (end-to-end growth support)
- 4+ AI Workers
- typically $10k+ / month
- used when teams want to run multiple channels and automate a bigger part of execution

The right setup really depends on where you’re trying to move the needle (CAC, volume, speed, etc.), so these are just benchmarks.

If helpful, we can quickly map this to what Wype is doing today and narrow it down to a much tighter range - no more than 15 mins.

Warmly,

Hanna Liakh

Hey David,

That actually makes total sense - and honestly, you’re already in a pretty clean setup (Apollo + HubSpot is a good base, I use it too :) ).

Where we usually come in is not by adding *more tools*, but by turning what you already have into a system that actually runs:

- deciding who to reach out to and how

- personalizing messaging based on signals

- triggering outreach + follow-ups automatically

So instead of “more outbound effort,” it becomes a bit more like *managed outbound*.

Out of curiosity - what’s the biggest bottleneck for you right now?

Is it more around:

- finding the right people

- writing custom messages per each lead

- or staying consistent with follow-ups?

Happy to show you how this could look in your setup if helpful - nothing heavy, just a quick walkthrough.

Hanna
